steelman: The TL design is a clean, defensible MVP architecture: contexts are split by business workstream (not tech layer), each aggregate owns one consistency boundary, and every component dependency resolves to a named contract. The hard correctness requirements from S1 are directly addressed — the last-item race is resolved at confirm by an atomic conditional decrement (ADR-002), totals are server-computed, idempotency is specified on confirm/refresh/capture/reserve, snapshots are immutable (ADR-003), and failure is handled by compensation rather than distributed rollback (ADR-004). The PCI boundary is confined to one service behind a swappable gateway (ADR-005), and audit is cross-cutting and append-only (ADR-006). The contracts carry non-vague idempotency rules, enumerated failure modes and explicit ordering guarantees with audit_id as the partition key. This is buildable as-is for the happy paths.

findings.claim: The checkout journey exhibits all three Orchestrator-instantiation signals (multi-aggregate: stock+order; compensation: release-on-failure; temporal: TTL) yet no standalone Orchestrator/saga is instantiated — orchestration is folded into checkout-service synchronously.
findings.evidence: ADR-007 + architecture_smells item 'Orchestrator instantiated…' = fail; component checkout-service parallel_safe:false with sync deps inventory.reserve + order.create.
findings.recommendation: Acceptable for a single-journey MVP IF crash-safety is proven (see RT-2); otherwise promote to a real Orchestrator with a saga log.

findings.claim: Dual writes are not atomic: a crash after inventory.reserve succeeds but before order.create / event publish leaves an orphan reservation and an at-risk domain event (DB commit and Kafka publish are separate).
findings.evidence: checkout.confirm makes sync inventory.reserve then order.create with events emitted directly; no transactional outbox in infra-summary/connectivity at round 1; ADR-004 TTL is only a time-bounded backstop, not atomicity.
findings.recommendation: Add a transactional outbox per producing service (event row committed in the same DB tx) + make order.create idempotent on confirm_id so checkout can safely retry after a crash. Keep TTL as the backstop.

findings.claim: Numeric SLO thresholds are absent, so the observability alerts and any latency gate cannot be wired meaningfully.
findings.evidence: observability-spec lists order-confirm p95 / listing latency as TBD-confirm-with-PM; S1 §3 names the signals without numbers.
findings.recommendation: Obtain numeric thresholds from PM (tracked as OQ-3); wire alerts once set. Non-blocking for build start.

findings.claim: The S1.5 UX pack is maturity 1 (brand tokens + all Thai microcopy TBD); fanning out frontend-implement before UX matures risks rework.
findings.evidence: S1.5 output.json maturity_level 1 with 4 P1 findings; S2 coverage_gaps carries the UX gaps forward.
findings.recommendation: Gate frontend-implement (S4b) on UX maturity ≥ 2; the backend path (S3/S4a) is unaffected and may proceed.

findings.claim: Catalog/cart routes (/, /products/:sku, /cart) have no BA story and no backend contract, so browse/cart behavior is unspecified for QA.
findings.evidence: S2 coverage_gaps kind ux_route_without_ba_story; no catalog/cart contract in api_contracts.
findings.recommendation: BA to confirm browse/cart scope and add stories/contracts or explicitly defer; flag for QA coverage.

bias_checks: Steelman written before findings (counters reject-by-default / self-preference bias).

Heterogeneity: author_model == critic_model (both Opus 4.8 authored the design and ran this review) — NOT a heterogeneous reviewer; confidence lowered accordingly and a true cross-model (Codex gpt-5.5 / Gemini) re-review is recommended for the real L3 gate.
Dropped 2 candidate findings as unfalsifiable/hallucinated: a vague 'Kafka may be overkill' (cost) and 'Redis SPOF' (not evidenced in the topology at this tier).
Each finding tied to concrete evidence in output.json / the ADRs; no position/verbosity-driven inflation.
